A defensible proposal is to preregister a small search: for two fixed models, evaluate shared blend weights α ∈ {0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1}, with score normalization and tie handling fixed beforehand. Select by equally weighted macro validation HR@10; retain all configurations’ category scores and prefer simpler weights on ties. Shared weights pool evidence across 800 users. Per-dataset weights adapt to domain differences but each uses only 200 users; five choices per category implicitly permit 625 weight vectors, increasing selection flexibility. Treat these as exploratory, or prespecify a small number of deviations toward category-specific weights. Small searches still risk overfitting the selection criterion. [Cawley and Talbot](https://www.jmlr.org/papers/v11/cawley10a.html)

For uncertainty, retain each user’s binary hit outcome for every configuration. Run, for example, 10,000 stratified paired bootstrap replicates: independently resample 200 users within each category, use identical sampled indices for both compared configurations, then average the four category differences. Report the observed macro difference and a descriptive 95% percentile interval. Keep each user’s fixed 99-negative candidate set intact; candidates are not independent observations. This estimates user-sampling uncertainty conditional on the trained models and candidate sets, excluding training-seed and negative-sampling variability. [Model-evaluation review](https://arxiv.org/abs/1811.12808)

Bootstrapping the selected winner against baseline holds its identity fixed and reuses the observations that made it win. It therefore does not remove validation-selection optimism or provide selection-adjusted coverage. Label those gains exploratory; independent held-out evaluation, or outer evaluation that repeats the complete selection procedure internally, is needed to assess the selected procedure. Preserve the pinned benchmark splits. [Selection-bias analysis](https://www.jmlr.org/papers/v11/cawley10a.html)
